summary: Two brick towers on a marsh island: an 1827 stump and an 1857 first-order tower that leans. Dark since 1947, now a federal wildlife refuge reachable only by boat.

access.note: Island in a national wildlife refuge, reachable only by boat; towers closed; landing only on occasional guided tours.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: first lighting 1827 (NRHP, LF) vs 1828 (Bulletin 1931); first-tower cost ($7,475+$950 NRHP vs $12,001 LF); funding year (1823 NRHP vs 1825 society); 1931 candlepower (390,000 Bulletin vs 430,000 LF); Johnson relieved at about 8:30 (Phoenix) vs 9 pm (LF, Digest); Johnson as assistant from 1867 (Digest) vs head keeper (roster); what remains of the dwellings (NRHP says destroyed 1947, LF says foundations remain). The 1886 earthquake and 1852 request are cited as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the Lighthouse Board report itself is not in the corpus for 1886/1852. The 1916 Bulletin rescue date is July 16 with the year taken from the Bulletin volume; the 1919 Bulletin's November 2-3 date is likewise from the volume year. Bulletin 1931 OCR of the lean-discovery year is garbled and was not used. Roster lines are copied from the USLHS archive, not independently confirmed; a few early-roster date ranges may be wrong. The Wichmann family anecdote is from one copyrighted source and paraphrased. Tour frequency varies by source (a handful / four / six per year). Bulletin 1931 also gives the old tower as about 80 ft (NRHP and LighthouseFriends: 65 ft), the light as 154 ft above water (NRHP: focal plane 161 ft), and says the lean was first noticed in 1869 (OCR partly garbled, not used). The 1919 Silsbie date (2-3 November) is from the Bulletin text.
